units.title: Aprender y adaptarte
units.goal: Explicar hábitos, cambios y estrategias de aprendizaje con razones.

rules.title: Hábitos frente a cambios
rules.text: Present simple describe rutinas; present continuous presenta cambios en desarrollo o situaciones temporales. No decidas solo por una palabra como now: piensa si describes una costumbre o un proceso.
examples: I practise a little every day.
My listening is improving this term.
I am taking an evening course.
rules.tip: Con he o she añade -s en presente simple; el continuo necesita be.

rules.title: Estados y esfuerzo
rules.text: Know, believe y understand suelen ir en presente simple. Manage to + infinitivo expresa que logras algo difícil; struggle with + nombre indica dificultad. Añade una estrategia para explicar cómo afrontas el problema.
rules.pattern: understand / manage to + verbo / struggle with + nombre
examples: I understand the main idea.
I managed to finish the task.
I struggle with long instructions.
rules.tip: No digas I am knowing. Para progreso puedes decir I am learning.

rules.title: Ampliar una respuesta
rules.text: Organiza tu respuesta: dificultad, ejemplo, estrategia y resultado. Because introduce la razón; so introduce la consecuencia. Evita unir todas las ideas solo con and.
examples: I take notes because they help me remember.
The task was difficult, so I asked for help.
For example, I review five words each morning.
rules.tip: Una respuesta B1 necesita detalles conectados, no una lista de frases aisladas.

questions.why: Un cambio en desarrollo se expresa con be + -ing.

questions.prompt: We managed ___ the project on time.
questions.why: Manage va seguido de to + infinitivo.

questions.prompt: I review words ___ I forget them easily.
I missed the explanation, ___ I asked a question.
questions.why: La segunda parte es una consecuencia.

units.story: When Diego joined an evening English class, he could understand short messages but struggled with longer conversations. At first, he tried to write down every word. This made him tired, and he often missed the main idea. His teacher suggested listening once without taking notes. Diego now writes three key words after each recording and explains the message to a partner. He still makes mistakes, but he is becoming more confident. Last week, he managed to understand a visitor's question at work without asking a colleague for help.

reading.prompt: Why did Diego change his method?
reading.answer: Writing every word made listening harder.
options: Writing every word made listening harder.
reading.why: Tomar demasiados apuntes le hacía perder la idea principal.

reading.prompt: What shows his progress?
reading.answer: He understood a visitor without help.
options: He understood a visitor without help.
reading.why: El último ejemplo muestra autonomía, no perfección.

dialogue: What are you doing about it?
I listen for the main idea first.
Yes, I feel more confident now.
units.writing: Escribe 80–110 palabras sobre una dificultad al aprender, una estrategia y un resultado concreto. Incluye because, so y un ejemplo.
units.model: I enjoy learning English, but I sometimes struggle with listening. I used to stop a recording whenever I heard a new word. Now I listen to the whole message first. Then I replay it and write down useful phrases. I practise for fifteen minutes after dinner because that is a quiet time at home. Last week, I understood the main idea of a short interview. I still need more practice, so I am keeping a small notebook to record my progress.

listening.text: Hello everyone. Our study group is moving to room twelve because the library is being painted. We will meet on Wednesday at six, not Thursday. Please bring a short recording that you find difficult. We will listen for the main idea before checking individual words. You do not need to print anything.

questions.why: El mensaje cambia la reunión a room twelve.
Se solicita un audio que resulte difícil.

units.mission: Habla 60–90 segundos sobre tu aprendizaje. Da una dificultad, un ejemplo y dos estrategias; responde a una pregunta de seguimiento.

units.title: Contar una historia
units.goal: Narrar una experiencia distinguiendo la acción principal, el contexto y un hecho anterior.

rules.title: Acciones y contexto
rules.text: Past simple hace avanzar la historia. Past continuous, was/were + -ing, describe el contexto o una acción en curso interrumpida por otra. When puede introducir el hecho breve; while suele acompañar la acción en desarrollo.
examples: I was waiting when the train arrived.
While we were travelling, it started to snow.
We found a seat near the window.
rules.tip: No todas las acciones largas necesitan continuo: importa cómo las presentas.

rules.title: Un pasado anterior
rules.text: Past perfect, had + participio, permite aclarar qué ocurrió antes de otro momento pasado. Una vez clara la secuencia, puedes continuar con past simple. No necesitas usar had en cada frase.
examples: The train had left before we arrived.
I realised that I had lost my ticket.
She had never travelled alone before.
rules.tip: Had no cambia con la persona; el participio de leave es left.

rules.title: Secuenciar y cerrar
rules.text: Presenta lugar y momento, explica el problema y termina con el resultado. At first contrasta con later o eventually. Fortunately comenta un resultado favorable; relieved describe cómo se sintió alguien.
examples: At first, I did not know what to do.
Eventually, a member of staff helped us.
I felt relieved because my bag was safe.
rules.tip: Eventually significa finalmente, no eventualmente en el sentido de quizá.

questions.prompt: I ___ for the bus when my phone rang.
While they ___, the lights went out.
When we arrived, the train ___ already left.
questions.why: El tren salió antes de nuestra llegada.

questions.prompt: She realised she had ___ her keys.
___, someone found my bag and returned it.
questions.why: La devolución fue un resultado favorable.

questions.prompt: Elige el cierre de una historia.

units.story: Maya was travelling to visit a friend when she realised that her phone was missing. She had used it in the station café, but she could not remember putting it back in her bag. By the time she returned, another customer was sitting at her table. Fortunately, the customer had given the phone to a waiter. Maya thanked them both and hurried to the platform. She missed her original train, but the next one left only twenty minutes later. Eventually, she arrived late but relieved, with a story to tell.

reading.prompt: Where had Maya last used her phone?
reading.why: El texto identifica el café.

reading.prompt: What happened as a result of returning?
reading.why: Pudo tomar otro tren veinte minutos después.

dialogue: I had left my phone in the café.
Yes, a waiter had kept it safe.
I caught the next train and called my friend.
units.writing: Escribe una historia de 90–120 palabras con contexto, problema y desenlace. Usa pasado simple, continuo y al menos un pasado perfecto.
units.model: Last Saturday, I was walking to a concert when I noticed that my ticket was not in my pocket. I had left it on the kitchen table. At first, I thought I would miss the performance. Then I remembered that my sister was still at home. I called her and asked for a photo of the ticket. Fortunately, the venue accepted the code on my phone. I arrived just before the music started. I felt very relieved, and I checked my pockets carefully before leaving the concert.

listening.text: This is a message for passengers on the service to Riverside. The train was delayed because a fallen tree had blocked the track. The track is now clear. We expect to leave in fifteen minutes from platform four. Please keep your tickets ready. Refreshments are available in the waiting room at no extra charge.

questions.answer: A tree had blocked the track.
options: A tree had blocked the track.

questions.prompt: Which platform will the train use?

questions.why: At no extra charge se refiere a refreshments.

units.mission: Cuenta una experiencia inesperada durante 90 segundos. Tu interlocutor pregunta qué había ocurrido antes del problema.

units.title: Experiencias y resultados
units.goal: Relacionar experiencias con el presente y pedir detalles sobre momentos terminados.

rules.title: Conexión con el presente
rules.text: Present perfect usa have/has + participio para experiencias o resultados relevantes ahora sin un momento pasado terminado. Past simple cuenta cuándo ocurrió un hecho: yesterday, in 2022 o last month.
examples: I have taken part in two projects.
We finished the first project last May.
Have you ever worked with children?
rules.tip: No combines present perfect con yesterday para una acción terminada.

rules.title: Duración y novedades
rules.text: For introduce una duración y since el punto inicial. Already suele situarse antes del participio; yet al final de preguntas o negativas. Gone significa que alguien se ha ido; been puede indicar una visita completada.
rules.pattern: for two years / since May / not… yet
examples: I have known Sara for three years.
She has lived here since April.
We have not received a reply yet.
rules.tip: Con estados como know se usa normalmente perfect simple, no continuo.

rules.title: Preguntar más
rules.text: Empieza con una pregunta de experiencia y continúa en past simple para conseguir detalles. Explica el resultado actual con so o as a result.
rules.pattern: Have you ever…? → When did you…?
examples: Have you ever organised an event?
When did you organise it?
I have gained experience, so I feel ready.
rules.tip: La conversación cambia de tiempo cuando pasa de experiencia general a un hecho concreto.

questions.why: So far conecta el periodo con el presente.
Last June es un periodo terminado.

questions.prompt: I have known him ___ ten years.

questions.why: El seguimiento pide un momento concreto en pasado.

units.story: Leo has volunteered at a community garden for two years. He first joined because he wanted to meet people outside his college. Since then, he has learnt how to grow vegetables and organise weekend activities. Last month, he helped run a workshop for new members. He was nervous at first, but the visitors asked interesting questions and seemed pleased with his explanations. Leo has recently applied for a summer job at a visitor centre. He has not received a reply yet, but he can now describe useful experience in his application.

reading.prompt: Why did Leo first join?
reading.why: Su motivo inicial era social.

reading.prompt: How can the garden experience help him now?
reading.answer: It gives examples for a job application.
options: It gives examples for a job application.
It means he needs no interview.
reading.why: El texto no promete que conseguirá el empleo.

dialogue: Have you ever led a workshop?
Yes, I led one last month.
How long have you volunteered there?
I have volunteered there for two years.
Have you received a job offer yet?
Not yet, but I have sent my application.
units.writing: Escribe 80–110 palabras sobre una experiencia que te haya enseñado algo. Separa la experiencia general de un hecho con fecha.
units.model: I have been a member of our photography club for a year. During that time, I have learnt to plan projects and explain my ideas. Last month, we prepared an exhibition about our neighbourhood. I took photos of local shops and interviewed two owners. At first, I was nervous about asking questions, but both people were friendly. We displayed the photos in the library. I have not sold any photographs yet, but this experience has made me more confident about working with other people.

listening.text: Hi, this is Nina from the volunteer team. We have received your application, but we have not received your reference yet. Please ask your teacher to email it before Friday. We have already arranged the interviews. Yours is on Monday morning at ten. Let us know if you need a different time.

questions.why: La solicitud llegó; la referencia no.
Se da el límite before Friday.
El mensaje confirma Monday morning at ten.

units.mission: Explica dos experiencias y responde cuándo, dónde y qué aprendiste en una de ellas.

units.title: Esfuerzos que continúan
units.goal: Expresar duración, actividad reciente y resultados cuantificables.

rules.title: Actividad hasta ahora
rules.text: Present perfect continuous: have/has been + -ing. Destaca duración o actividad reciente que explica una situación actual. Puede seguir ocurriendo o acabar de terminar; el contexto lo aclara.
examples: I have been working on my project all morning.
She has been learning English since January.
We have been waiting for an hour.
rules.tip: No omitas been; have working no es correcto.

rules.title: Actividad o cantidad
rules.text: Perfect simple suele destacar resultados terminados o cuántos: I have written three pages. Perfect continuous destaca el proceso: I have been writing. Con know, own y believe normalmente usa simple.
rules.pattern: How many have you…? / How long have you been…?
examples: I have written three pages.
How long have you been studying?
I have known her since school.
rules.tip: Una actividad larga no obliga al continuo si el verbo expresa un estado.

rules.title: Explicar un problema
rules.text: Di qué llevas haciendo, cómo te afecta y qué necesitas. Una petición concreta permite que la otra persona te ayude.
examples: I have been looking at the screen for hours.
I feel tired, so I need a short break.
Could you check this paragraph for me?
rules.tip: Usa for con duración y since con el inicio.

questions.why: La cantidad terminada destaca el resultado.

questions.prompt: How ___ have you been working on this?
I have ___ this teacher for years.
I am tired because I ___ all morning.
questions.why: La actividad reciente explica el cansancio.

units.story: Amira and Tom have been preparing a local history podcast for three weeks. They have interviewed four neighbours and collected some old photographs. Amira has been editing the recordings, while Tom has been checking dates in the library. They planned to finish yesterday, but one interview was difficult to hear. Instead of using unclear audio, they asked the speaker to record a few sentences again. They have now completed the first episode. Although the project has taken longer than expected, both students think the extra care has improved the result.

reading.prompt: Why did the project take longer?
reading.why: Tuvieron que repetir parte de una grabación.

reading.prompt: What have they completed?
reading.why: El resultado concreto es el primer episodio.

dialogue: How long have you been editing?
I have been editing since breakfast.
I have finished the first five minutes.
Why are you taking a break?
I have been concentrating for hours.
units.writing: Escribe una actualización de proyecto de 80–110 palabras: duración, dos resultados y un problema con su siguiente paso.
units.model: Our team has been preparing a short video for two weeks. We have written the script and filmed three scenes. I have been editing the sound, which is more difficult than I expected. The street was noisy when we filmed the final scene, so some words are unclear. We are going to record those lines again tomorrow. Although we have not finished the video yet, we are making progress. We need one more afternoon to check the result before showing it to our class.

listening.text: Quick project update: we have been testing the new website since Tuesday. We have fixed the sign-in page and the search button. The photo gallery is still slow, so please do not upload new images yet. We will test it again tomorrow afternoon and send another update by five.

questions.prompt: What should users avoid for now?
questions.why: Se pide no subir nuevas imágenes todavía.

units.mission: Da una actualización oral de un proyecto real o imaginario: cuánto tiempo, qué has terminado y qué falta.

units.title: Antes y ahora
units.goal: Comparar hábitos anteriores con nuevas situaciones y procesos de adaptación.

rules.title: Costumbres que cambiaron
rules.text: Used to + infinitivo describe hábitos o estados pasados que ya no son ciertos. En preguntas y negativas con did se usa use to. Past simple también puede describir hábitos si el contexto es claro.
rules.pattern: used to + verbo / did not use to
examples: I used to live near the sea.
She did not use to drive to work.
Did you use to share a room?
rules.tip: No escribas did you used to en la forma estándar.

rules.title: Estar o llegar a estar acostumbrado
rules.text: Be used to significa estar acostumbrado. Get used to describe la adaptación. Aquí to es una preposición: después usa un nombre o -ing, no un infinitivo.
examples: I am used to the noise now.
She is getting used to travelling alone.
We are not used to waking up early.
rules.tip: I used to work y I am used to working tienen significados diferentes.

rules.title: Comparar con equilibrio
rules.text: Describe una ventaja y una dificultad. Whereas contrasta dos situaciones; however inicia una idea que limita o contrasta la anterior. Añade un ejemplo personal.
examples: My old town was quiet, whereas this city is busy.
However, there are more opportunities here.
I still miss my old neighbours.
rules.tip: Separa however con puntuación cuando conecta oraciones completas.

questions.prompt: I ___ walk to school, but now I take a bus.
questions.why: Se trata de un hábito que cambió.
To es preposición en be used to.

questions.prompt: She is getting used to the city. Esto significa:
options: Vivía allí antes, pero ya no.
questions.why: Get used to describe un proceso.

questions.prompt: The village was quiet, ___ the city is noisy.
I did not ___ enjoy long journeys.
questions.why: La negativa con did usa la forma base.

units.story: When Tomas moved from a small town to the capital, the morning journey was the hardest change. He used to walk to college in ten minutes, but now he spends almost an hour on a bus. At first, he tried to read during the journey and felt uncomfortable. He is getting used to listening to podcasts instead. He still misses the quiet streets near his old home. However, he has joined a music group and enjoys meeting people from different places. He says the city feels less strange each week.

reading.prompt: What changed most for Tomas?
reading.answer: His journey to college became longer.
options: His journey to college became longer.
reading.why: El cambio difícil fue el trayecto.

reading.prompt: How does he feel about the city now?
reading.why: Hay dificultades y también nuevas relaciones.

dialogue: Did you use to live nearby?
No, I used to live in a small town.
Are you used to the buses now?
I am getting used to them.
units.writing: Compara tu vida antes y ahora en 80–110 palabras. Incluye used to y be/get used to con estructuras distintas.
units.model: I used to study in a small school where everyone knew my name. This year, I moved to a larger college. At first, I got lost between classes and missed my old friends. I am getting used to the building now, and I have joined a sports club. I am also used to planning my own study time, which was difficult in the beginning. My old school felt more familiar, whereas the new college offers more activities. I still visit my old friends at weekends.

listening.text: Welcome to your new residence. Some of you may not be used to sharing a kitchen. Please label your food and clean the table after eating. The quiet period begins at ten in the evening. If you need help settling in, our student adviser is available downstairs every Tuesday afternoon.

questions.why: El mensaje trata la cocina compartida.

questions.prompt: When does the quiet period begin?
questions.why: Se anuncia ten in the evening.
La persona está disponible los martes.

units.mission: Compara dos etapas de tu vida. Explica qué era diferente y a qué te estás acostumbrando.

units.title: Planes y decisiones
units.goal: Distinguir intenciones, acuerdos, decisiones y condiciones temporales futuras.

rules.title: Elegir la forma de futuro
rules.text: Going to expresa intenciones previas o predicciones con evidencia; present continuous se usa para acuerdos organizados. Will puede expresar una decisión en el momento, una oferta o una predicción. El significado y el contexto importan.
examples: We are going to organise a trip.
I am meeting the guide at nine tomorrow.
I will carry that bag for you.
rules.tip: No todas las frases futuras tienen una sola forma posible fuera de contexto.

rules.title: Después de when y as soon as
rules.text: En cláusulas temporales de futuro usa normalmente presente simple después de when, as soon as, before y until. La cláusula principal puede llevar will. Until indica que algo continúa hasta un punto.
examples: I will call you when I arrive.
We will leave as soon as everyone is ready.
Wait here until the bus comes.
rules.tip: Evita when I will arrive en este tipo de cláusula temporal.

rules.title: Organizar una alternativa
rules.text: Propón hora y lugar, confirma disponibilidad y acuerda qué hacer si cambia la situación. Resume el acuerdo al final para evitar malentendidos.
examples: Are you available on Friday afternoon?
Shall we meet outside the museum?
If it rains, we will choose an indoor activity.
rules.tip: Una invitación clara incluye cuándo, dónde y cómo confirmar.

questions.prompt: I promise I ___ send the details tonight.
questions.why: Will se usa para la promesa.

questions.prompt: We have tickets; we ___ the guide tomorrow.
questions.why: El acuerdo futuro admite presente continuo.

questions.prompt: I will text you when I ___.
We will start as soon as Sara ___ ready.
questions.why: As soon as + presente para futuro.

questions.prompt: ___ we meet at the main entrance?
questions.why: Shall we propone una acción conjunta.
Until marca el final de la espera.

units.story: Our class is planning a visit to a science museum next Friday. We have already booked the coach, and we are meeting outside college at eight. The museum has asked us to confirm the number of visitors two days in advance. Some students want to bring lunch, while others prefer the café. Our teacher will send a message as soon as the final schedule is ready. If the weather is good, we will eat in the gardens. Otherwise, the museum has offered us a room inside. Everyone must confirm by Tuesday.

reading.prompt: What has already been organised?
reading.why: Se ha reservado el transporte.

reading.prompt: Why should students reply by Tuesday?
reading.answer: The museum needs visitor numbers in advance.
options: The museum needs visitor numbers in advance.
The museum closes forever on Wednesday.
reading.why: Se necesita confirmar la cantidad de visitantes.

dialogue: Are you free on Friday morning?
Yes, I am meeting the group at eight.
We will eat inside the museum.
When will you send the schedule?
I will send it as soon as it is ready.
units.writing: Escribe un correo de 90–120 palabras organizando una salida: acuerdo, detalles pendientes, alternativa y confirmación.
units.model: Hi everyone, we are visiting the river park on Saturday, and I have booked a table at the café for lunch. We are meeting at the main entrance at ten. Please bring comfortable shoes because we are going to walk along the river first. If it rains, we will visit the nearby art gallery instead. I will send the exact route as soon as the café confirms our booking. Could you let me know by Thursday whether you can come? I hope to see you there. Best, Elena

listening.text: Hi, it is Jo. Our guide has changed Saturday's meeting place. We are still meeting at nine, but please go to the side entrance rather than the main gate. I will message you as soon as I get there. If you are running late, call me before the tour starts.

questions.why: La hora y el día se mantienen.
Se contrasta side entrance con main gate.

questions.prompt: What should a late person do?
questions.why: Se pide una llamada antes del comienzo.

units.mission: Organiza una salida con otra persona. Propón dos opciones, acuerda una y explica un plan alternativo.

units.title: Condiciones y consecuencias
units.goal: Explicar resultados habituales y posibilidades futuras con condiciones.

rules.title: Hechos habituales
rules.text: Zero conditional suele usar presente en ambas partes para relaciones habituales. No expresa necesariamente una ley científica: también puede describir tu rutina. La condición puede aparecer al principio o al final.
examples: If I sleep badly, I feel tired.
Plants grow better if they get enough light.
If the bus is full, I walk.
rules.tip: Pon coma después de la condición cuando va al principio.

rules.title: Futuro posible
rules.text: First conditional: if + presente, will + infinitivo. Sirve para una condición futura considerada posible. La consecuencia también admite can, might o un imperativo según la intención. Unless equivale aproximadamente a if not.
examples: If it rains, we will stay inside.
We will miss the train unless we leave now.
If you need help, call me.
rules.tip: No pongas will automáticamente en la parte con if.

rules.title: Preparación frente a condición
rules.text: In case expresa precaución: llevas el paraguas ahora por la posibilidad de lluvia. If it rains expresa una acción dependiente de que llueva. No son siempre intercambiables.
examples: Take a jacket in case it gets cold.
If it gets cold, I will go inside.
We should prepare an alternative.
rules.tip: Distingue prepararte antes de un problema y reaccionar cuando ocurre.

questions.prompt: If I miss breakfast, I usually ___ hungry by ten.
If it rains tomorrow, we ___ indoors.
Take water ___ the shop is closed.

questions.why: La consecuencia puede ser un imperativo.

units.story: A group of friends is organising a walk in the hills. They have checked the route, but the forecast may change. If heavy rain is expected, they will postpone the walk. If there is only light rain, they will choose a shorter path near the village. Everyone will carry water in case the café is closed. The organiser has asked each person to bring a charged phone. They will not leave unless everyone has suitable shoes. The aim is to enjoy the day without taking unnecessary risks.

reading.prompt: What will happen in heavy rain?
options: They will take a longer route.
reading.why: El plan depende de la intensidad de la lluvia.

reading.prompt: Why will they carry water?
reading.why: In case expresa precaución.

dialogue: What will we do if it rains?
We will choose the shorter route.
Yes, in case the café is closed.
Not unless everyone has suitable shoes.
units.writing: Escribe 80–110 palabras con un plan al aire libre, dos condiciones, una precaución y la razón de cada decisión.
units.model: We are planning a picnic by the lake on Sunday. If the weather is warm, we will swim in the supervised area. If it rains heavily, we will have lunch at my house instead. Please bring a warm top in case the temperature falls later. We will not start cooking unless everyone has arrived, so let me know if you are delayed. I will bring drinking water because the nearest shop is quite far away. With these alternatives, we should still have a good day.

listening.text: For tomorrow's outdoor class, bring a notebook in case the tablets stop working. If it rains, we will use room six. The lesson will start at the usual time, half past nine. Unless you receive a message tonight, please come to the garden entrance first.

questions.prompt: Where will the lesson be in rain?
questions.why: El número de sala es six.

units.mission: Negocia un plan y responde a tres preguntas que empiecen con What will you do if…?

units.title: Situaciones imaginarias
units.goal: Explorar situaciones hipotéticas y dar consejos razonados.

rules.title: Segunda condicional
rules.text: If + pasado simple, would + infinitivo presenta una situación imaginaria o poco probable en presente o futuro. El pasado aquí señala distancia de la realidad, no necesariamente tiempo pasado.
examples: If I had more time, I would learn to cook.
I would travel more if tickets were cheaper.
What would you do if you lost your phone?
rules.tip: No pongas would en ambas partes de la estructura básica.

rules.title: Consejo y posibilidades
rules.text: If I were you es una expresión frecuente para aconsejar. Could expresa una opción o capacidad hipotética; might una posibilidad menos segura. Would indica el resultado imaginado, no una certeza real.
rules.pattern: If I were you, I would…
examples: If I were you, I would ask for advice.
We could rent bikes if we stayed longer.
I might join if I knew someone there.
rules.tip: Were se usa habitualmente en If I were you.

rules.title: Valorar alternativas
rules.text: Explica el beneficio, reconoce una dificultad y justifica tu elección. On the other hand permite presentar el otro lado de una decisión.
rules.pattern: one advantage / on the other hand
examples: One advantage would be more free time.
On the other hand, it would cost more.
I would choose the first option because it is practical.
rules.tip: No basta con elegir: añade una razón relacionada con el problema.

questions.prompt: If I had a bike, I ___ to college.
If she ___ more time, she would help.
If I ___ you, I would talk to the teacher.
questions.why: Es la expresión habitual de consejo.

questions.prompt: We ___ visit both places if we stayed longer.
What would you do if you ___ your keys?
questions.why: La parte con if usa pasado.

questions.prompt: Para presentar una desventaja tras una ventaja:
questions.why: La expresión introduce la otra perspectiva.

units.story: A neighbourhood group has been given a small empty building. Some members would turn it into a study room if they could find enough desks. Others would prefer a workshop where people could repair bicycles. Both ideas would help local residents, but the group cannot afford to do everything at once. Ana suggests opening a study room first because volunteers have already offered furniture. If the group earned money from weekend events, it could add the workshop later. The members agree to ask residents what they need before making a final decision.

reading.prompt: Why does Ana suggest a study room first?
reading.why: Su argumento se basa en recursos disponibles.

reading.prompt: What will the group do before deciding?
reading.why: Quieren conocer las necesidades.

dialogue: What would you do with the building?
I would open a study room.
What would be the main benefit?
Students would have a quiet place.
We would need volunteers to keep it open.
units.writing: Escribe 90–120 palabras sobre cómo mejorarías un espacio de tu comunidad. Explica dos ventajas y una dificultad.
units.model: If I could improve one place in my neighbourhood, I would change the empty space beside the library into a small garden. People could sit there and read, and children would have a safer place to meet. I would ask local residents to help choose the plants. One difficulty would be keeping the area clean. If volunteers shared the work, however, it would be easier. I would start with a few benches and simple plants rather than spending all the money at once.

listening.text: If I were in charge of the club budget, I would buy second-hand instruments first. New equipment would be wonderful, but it would leave no money for lessons. We could ask experienced members to check the instruments before we buy them. That would reduce the risk of choosing something damaged.

questions.prompt: What problem would new equipment create?
questions.answer: No money would remain for lessons.
options: No money would remain for lessons.
The club would need no teachers.

questions.why: Se propone ayuda de personas con experiencia.

units.mission: Responde qué harías con un espacio o presupuesto limitado. Compara dos alternativas y justifica tu elección.

units.title: Obligaciones y consejos
units.goal: Distinguir obligaciones, prohibiciones, opciones y recomendaciones.

rules.title: Obligación y prohibición
rules.text: Must y have to expresan obligación; must not expresa prohibición. Do not have to significa ausencia de obligación: puedes hacerlo si quieres. Para obligación pasada se usa had to.
rules.pattern: must / have to / must not / do not have to
examples: You must wear closed shoes.
You must not touch the equipment.
We had to show our tickets.
rules.tip: Do not have to no significa prohibido.

rules.title: Consejos y permisos
rules.text: Should aconseja; could ofrece una opción menos directa. Be allowed to expresa permiso y funciona en distintos tiempos. Para pedir permiso usa Can I…? o Could I…?
rules.pattern: should + verbo / be allowed to + verbo
examples: You should read the instructions first.
You could ask a member of staff.
Visitors are allowed to take photographs.
rules.tip: Después de should no pongas to.

rules.title: Explicar el motivo
rules.text: Una instrucción resulta más clara si incluyes su finalidad. So that + oración explica el objetivo; to + infinitivo también puede expresar propósito.
examples: Keep the door clear so that people can leave.
Wear gloves to protect your hands.
Please ask if any rule is unclear.
rules.tip: Distingue una norma obligatoria de una sugerencia en el tono y el vocabulario.

questions.prompt: You do not have to bring food means:

questions.why: La obligación pasada usa had to.
So that introduce la finalidad con sujeto y verbo.

units.story: Before joining a pottery workshop, visitors receive a short safety guide. They must wear closed shoes and tie back long hair. They must not use the large oven themselves; only trained staff are allowed to operate it. Participants do not have to bring tools because everything is provided. The instructor recommends bringing an old shirt, although this is optional. During the first lesson, everyone practises shaping a small bowl. The rules help beginners feel confident because they know which tasks they can try alone and when they should ask for assistance.

reading.prompt: Which task is restricted to trained staff?
reading.why: La restricción es específica.

reading.prompt: Do participants need their own tools?
options: Yes, every person must buy them.
Only if they wear closed shoes.
reading.why: No tienen que traer herramientas.

dialogue: Do I have to bring any tools?
Only trained staff are allowed to use it.
Should I bring an old shirt?
Yes, that would be a good idea.
units.writing: Escribe una guía de 80–110 palabras para una actividad. Incluye dos obligaciones, una prohibición, una opción y un consejo.
units.model: Welcome to our community kitchen. Everyone must wash their hands before preparing food, and you have to keep your working area clean. You must not use the large mixer until a supervisor has shown you how it works. You do not have to bring your own apron because we can lend you one. However, you should wear comfortable shoes. Please keep bags away from the doors so that people can move safely. If you are unsure about any equipment, ask a member of the team for help.

listening.text: For today's museum visit, you must keep your ticket with you. You are allowed to take photos without flash in the main galleries, but photography is prohibited in the special exhibition. You do not have to leave small bags at the entrance. Large backpacks, however, must go in a locker.

questions.prompt: What must happen to large backpacks?
questions.answer: They must go in a locker.
options: They must go in a locker.
questions.why: Hay una norma para mochilas grandes.
Do not have to elimina la obligación.

units.mission: Explica normas a una persona nueva y responde qué es obligatorio, opcional y prohibido.

units.title: Deducir con prudencia
units.goal: Expresar certeza y posibilidad a partir de indicios sin confundirlas con hechos.

rules.title: Deducciones presentes
rules.text: Must + infinitivo puede expresar una deducción fuerte. Cannot o can’t expresa que algo parece imposible. Aquí must no es una orden: el contexto distingue ambos usos.
examples: The lights are on; someone must be home.
That cannot be our bus; the number is wrong.
She must be tired after such a long walk.
rules.tip: Una deducción sigue dependiendo de la calidad de los indicios.

rules.title: Posibilidad
rules.text: May, might y could expresan posibilidad. Might not significa quizá no; no equivale a cannot. Usa be + -ing después del modal para una actividad en curso.
examples: He might be working upstairs.
The shop may be closed today.
They could be waiting at the other entrance.
rules.tip: Evita añadir -s al verbo después de un modal.

rules.title: Comprobar antes de afirmar
rules.text: Separa observación, interpretación y verificación. It seems that suaviza una conclusión; let us check propone buscar información.
examples: The screen is dark, but the battery might be empty.
It seems that the meeting has moved.
Let us check before we tell everyone.
rules.tip: No presentes una suposición como información confirmada.

questions.prompt: The number is different. This ___ be our bus.
She ___ be tired after walking all day.
questions.why: Must puede expresar una deducción fuerte.

questions.prompt: He is not answering. He might ___ sleeping.
questions.why: Después del modal va la base.

questions.prompt: They could ___ at the side entrance.

questions.answer: Check it before sharing it as fact.
options: Check it before sharing it as fact.

units.story: When the reading group arrived at the library, their usual room was dark and the door was locked. Ben said the meeting must be cancelled, but Aisha was not sure. The rest of the building was open, and she could hear voices upstairs. She suggested that the group might be using another room. They checked the noticeboard and found a message explaining that a pipe was being repaired. The meeting had moved to the second floor. Aisha was glad they had checked instead of going home immediately.

reading.prompt: Why was Ben's conclusion too quick?
reading.answer: He had not checked the other information.
options: He had not checked the other information.
reading.why: Había otras pistas por comprobar.

reading.prompt: What was the actual explanation?
reading.answer: The group had moved rooms because of repairs.
options: The group had moved rooms because of repairs.
The members had all gone home.
The library had lost every book.
reading.why: El aviso explicó el traslado.

dialogue: The room is empty. Has everyone left?
Let us check the noticeboard first.
units.writing: Describe en 80–110 palabras una situación confusa: dos posibles explicaciones, las pistas y cómo comprobarías lo ocurrido.
units.model: Yesterday, I arrived at the sports centre and found the swimming pool empty. At first, I thought it must be closed for the whole day. However, the changing rooms were still open, and several swimmers were waiting near reception. I realised there might be a short delay instead. I asked a member of staff before changing my plans. She explained that they were checking the water and expected to reopen in twenty minutes. I was pleased that I had checked rather than simply leaving.

listening.text: I cannot find the meeting invitation in my main inbox. It might be in the spam folder, or perhaps I used my other address when I registered. I will check both before contacting the organiser. The event cannot be tomorrow because the poster clearly says next Friday.

questions.prompt: What will the speaker do first?
Why cannot the event be tomorrow?
questions.why: El cartel aporta un dato concreto.

units.mission: Observa una escena y plantea dos hipótesis con might/could y una deducción con must o cannot. Explica los indicios.

units.title: Procesos y noticias
units.goal: Describir procesos y hechos poniendo el foco en la acción o el resultado.

rules.title: Pasiva presente y pasada
rules.text: La pasiva se forma con be + participio. Cambia be según el tiempo: is made, are made, was made, were made. Se usa cuando interesa la acción o no sabemos quién la realiza.
examples: The paper is collected every Friday.
These chairs were made locally.
The bridge was repaired last year.
rules.tip: El participio de make es made, no maked.

rules.title: Quién realiza la acción
rules.text: By introduce al agente si resulta importante. No es obligatorio añadirlo. La pasiva conserva el tiempo del hecho; el objeto de la activa pasa a ser sujeto de la pasiva.
rules.pattern: objeto de activa → sujeto de pasiva
examples: Local artists designed the posters.
The posters were designed by local artists.
The results are published online.
rules.tip: La pasiva no vuelve más verdadero un dato: comprueba siempre la fuente.

rules.title: Ordenar un proceso
rules.text: Usa first, next, then y finally para pasos. Explica el propósito de cada etapa cuando ayude al lector. Diferencia una descripción habitual de un hecho pasado.
examples: First, the bottles are sorted by colour.
Next, they are washed carefully.
Finally, the material is used to make new products.
rules.tip: Mantén el mismo tiempo cuando describes un proceso habitual.

questions.prompt: The bags ___ made from recycled paper.

questions.why: Bridge es singular y el hecho es pasado.

questions.prompt: Elige la pasiva de They collect the paper.
Para introducir el último paso usa:

units.story: A small company in Carla's town makes bags from old advertising banners. The banners are collected from local events and sorted according to their condition. They are then cleaned and cut into useful shapes. Each bag is sewn by a member of the workshop, so no two bags look exactly the same. The company was started by three friends who wanted to reduce waste. Last year, its products were sold at a regional craft fair. Customers liked the unusual colours and the explanation of where the material had come from.

reading.prompt: Why do the bags look different?
reading.answer: They use different pieces of old banners.
options: They use different pieces of old banners.
reading.why: Cada pieza de material es distinta.

reading.prompt: Why was the company started?
reading.why: El propósito era reutilizar materiales.

dialogue: What are these bags made from?
They are made from old banners.
They are collected after local events.
They are sewn by people in our workshop.
units.writing: Explica un proceso en 80–110 palabras: origen del material, tres pasos y uso final. Usa pasiva y conectores de orden.
units.model: At our school, used notebooks are collected at the end of each term. First, pages that have not been written on are separated from the rest. Next, they are cut to the same size and placed in small piles. The pages are then attached to covers made from old cardboard. Finally, the new notebooks are given to students for taking rough notes. The project was started by our environmental club. It saves useful paper and shows how simple materials can be used again instead of being thrown away.

listening.text: The new footbridge was opened this morning. It was designed by a local engineer and built using recycled steel. The old bridge was damaged in last winter's storms. The new path is open to walkers and cyclists, but motor vehicles are not allowed. Lighting will be checked during the first week.

questions.prompt: Why was the old bridge replaced?
questions.why: El daño ocurrió el invierno anterior.

questions.prompt: Who can use the new path?

units.mission: Explica cómo se fabrica o reutiliza un producto. Incluye cuatro pasos claros y quién participa cuando sea relevante.

units.title: Transmitir mensajes
units.goal: Resumir lo que otra persona dijo, pidió o preguntó.

rules.title: Afirmaciones indirectas
rules.text: Al relatar con said o told en pasado, suele retroceder el tiempo: am pasa a was, have a had, will a would. Si algo sigue siendo cierto puede mantenerse el presente; aquí practicamos el cambio habitual.
examples: She said that she was busy.
He told me that he would call later.
They said that they had finished.
rules.tip: Told suele necesitar a quién: told me. No digas said me.

rules.title: Preguntas y peticiones
rules.text: Las preguntas indirectas usan orden de afirmación. Para sí/no usa if o whether. Una petición se transmite con asked someone to + verbo; la negativa con not to.
rules.pattern: asked if + sujeto + verbo / asked me to
examples: She asked if I was free.
He asked where I lived.
They asked us not to make noise.
rules.tip: No mantengas do/does de la pregunta directa.

rules.title: Cambiar perspectiva
rules.text: Adapta pronombres, lugar y tiempo al contexto: tomorrow puede ser the following day si el relato ocurre después. Comprueba que el mensaje sigue teniendo sentido desde quien lo cuenta.
rules.pattern: I → he/she / tomorrow → the following day
examples: The guide said the tour would start the following day.
I told her that I needed more information.
Could you confirm that I understood correctly?
rules.tip: Los cambios de tiempo y lugar no son mecánicos si el contexto no cambia.

questions.prompt: She said she ___ tired. (Relato en pasado.)
He ___ me that he would call.

questions.why: La pregunta indirecta usa orden afirmativo.
If introduce la pregunta de sí/no.

questions.prompt: Please do not leave → She asked me ___.
questions.why: La petición negativa usa not to.

units.story: When the club organiser could not attend a meeting, he asked Priya to pass on a message. He said that the weekend event would begin an hour later than planned. He also asked members to bring reusable cups and not to park in front of the school gate. Priya wrote down the main points before speaking to the group. One member asked whether families were still welcome. Priya was not sure, so she said she would check instead of guessing. Later, the organiser confirmed that families could attend as usual.

reading.prompt: What changed about the event?
reading.answer: It would start an hour later.
options: It would start an hour later.
reading.why: El cambio confirmado era el horario.

reading.prompt: What did Priya do when unsure?
reading.why: Separó información confirmada de dudas.

dialogue: He said the event would start later.
Did he ask us to bring anything?
He asked us to bring reusable cups.
He confirmed that families could attend.
units.writing: Escribe un mensaje de 80–110 palabras transmitiendo tres indicaciones de otra persona. Incluye una pregunta pendiente y cómo la resolverás.
units.model: Hi everyone, I spoke to our teacher about Friday's visit. She said that we would leave at nine instead of half past eight. She asked us to bring our student cards and reminded us not to take large bags. I asked whether we needed to buy lunch, but she said she would check the café opening times first. She promised to send another message tomorrow. For now, please make sure you have your card ready. I will share the lunch information as soon as I receive it.

listening.text: I spoke to the coach this morning. She said that practice would be indoors because the field was wet. She asked us to bring clean trainers and told us not to arrive before four. I asked if we should bring a ball, and she said the club would provide everything else.

questions.why: No deben llegar antes de las cuatro.

units.mission: Transmite un aviso de otra persona sin leerlo literalmente. Comprueba con tu interlocutor que entiende las indicaciones.

units.title: Describir con precisión
units.goal: Identificar personas, objetos y lugares usando oraciones de relativo.

rules.title: Identificar con relativos
rules.text: Who se refiere a personas; which a cosas. That puede reemplazarlos en muchas relativas especificativas, sin comas. El relativo conecta información necesaria para identificar el referente.
examples: The woman who runs the café is my neighbour.
This is the book that I recommended.
I prefer places which have outdoor seating.
rules.tip: No repitas el sujeto: the woman who she runs es incorrecto.

rules.title: Lugar y posesión
rules.text: Where introduce una relación de lugar; whose expresa posesión y va seguido de un nombre. Puedes omitir un relativo objeto en una especificativa, pero no un relativo sujeto.
examples: This is the park where we met.
I know a student whose father is a pilot.
The film we watched was interesting.
rules.tip: En the person who called, who es sujeto y no se omite.

rules.title: Información adicional
rules.text: Las relativas explicativas añaden información con comas. Usa who o which, no that. En el habla, marca una pequeña pausa para que el oyente siga la descripción.
examples: My sister, who lives nearby, can help.
The museum, which opened last year, is popular.
It is the building next to the station.
rules.tip: Identificar y añadir información no son exactamente la misma función.

questions.prompt: The person ___ called is my teacher.
questions.why: Who se refiere a una persona.

questions.prompt: This is the café ___ we met.
questions.why: Where introduce el lugar del encuentro.

questions.prompt: I know a girl ___ brother is an artist.

questions.answer: The woman who works here is kind.
options: The woman who works here is kind.
The woman who she works here is kind.
The woman where works here is kind.

questions.prompt: My bike, ___ is quite old, still works.
questions.why: Con comas usa which para cosas.

questions.answer: That en the book that I bought.
options: That en the book that I bought.
Who en the woman who called.
Which en the bus which arrived.
questions.why: Solo es objeto en el primer ejemplo.

units.story: When Lina moved to a new district, she used landmarks to find her way around. The bakery that stayed open late became her favourite place to buy bread. Next to it was a small library where residents could borrow tools as well as books. Lina met a neighbour whose daughter organised walking tours. On one tour, she discovered an old cinema, which had recently become a community theatre. She realised that learning about the people who used these buildings made the area feel much more familiar than simply memorising street names.

reading.prompt: What was unusual about the library?
options: It was open only at night.
reading.why: Se prestaban herramientas además de libros.

reading.prompt: What helped Lina feel at home?
reading.answer: Learning about local people and places.
options: Learning about local people and places.
reading.why: El vínculo era social y geográfico.

dialogue: The one that used to be a cinema.
Yes, the library where you can borrow tools.
A neighbour whose daughter studies history.
units.writing: Describe tu barrio en 80–110 palabras. Usa who, where y whose para incluir personas y lugares.
units.model: The place I like most in my neighbourhood is a library that opens on Sundays. It has a quiet room where students can work together. The librarian, who knows many local families, often recommends books to new visitors. I also know a volunteer whose son teaches computer classes there. Last month, I joined a workshop and met several neighbours. The building is small, but it offers more than books. It is a place where people share useful skills and feel part of the community.

listening.text: The walking tour starts outside the theatre, which used to be a cinema. Look for a guide who is carrying a green folder. We will visit the market where local farmers sell produce. Anyone whose ticket includes lunch should stay with the group after the tour.

questions.why: El teatro es el punto inicial.

questions.prompt: How can visitors identify the guide?
questions.why: Se describe al guía con una carpeta.

questions.prompt: Who should stay after the tour?
questions.why: Whose ticket includes lunch identifica al grupo.

units.mission: Describe un lugar sin decir su nombre para que otra persona lo identifique. Incluye personas y funciones.

units.title: Elegir estructuras verbales
units.goal: Usar verbos con infinitivo o -ing en planes, preferencias y propósitos.

rules.title: Patrones frecuentes
rules.text: Enjoy, avoid, finish y consider suelen ir con -ing. Decide, hope, plan y offer suelen ir con to + infinitivo. Aprende cada verbo con su patrón dentro de una frase.
examples: I enjoy learning new skills.
We decided to join the class.
She offered to help us.
rules.tip: Evita I enjoy to learn en el inglés estándar.

rules.title: Preposiciones y propósito
rules.text: Después de una preposición, un verbo suele ir en -ing. Para expresar propósito usa to + infinitivo. Look forward to incluye una preposición, así que admite -ing.
examples: I am interested in studying abroad.
We met to discuss the plan.
I look forward to meeting you.
rules.tip: To no siempre marca infinitivo: depende de la estructura.

rules.title: Cambios de significado
rules.text: Stop doing significa dejar una actividad; stop to do significa parar otra actividad para hacer algo. Remember doing es recordar un hecho; remember to do es acordarse de realizar una tarea.
examples: He stopped talking when the film began.
We stopped to buy some water.
Remember to lock the door.
rules.tip: El significado decide la forma: no memorices solo una traducción.

units.story: Rosa wanted to learn a practical skill, so she considered joining a woodwork class. She enjoyed making small objects but avoided using unfamiliar tools. The instructor offered to show her the basic techniques before the first group lesson. Rosa agreed to attend and practised following simple instructions. During the class, she stopped to check each measurement rather than rushing. By the end, she had finished making a shelf. She was pleased with the result and looked forward to trying a more difficult project the following week.

reading.prompt: Why did the instructor offer help first?
reading.answer: Rosa was unsure about unfamiliar tools.
options: Rosa was unsure about unfamiliar tools.
Rosa wanted to teach the class.
reading.why: La ayuda preparó a la principiante.

reading.prompt: What did Rosa do instead of rushing?
reading.why: Su pausa tenía un propósito.

dialogue: I am considering joining a class.
I have decided to try woodwork.
Are you looking forward to it?
Yes, I enjoy making useful things.
units.writing: Escribe 80–110 palabras sobre una habilidad que quieras aprender. Incluye tres patrones verbales y un propósito.
units.model: I have decided to learn how to cook a few healthy meals. I enjoy watching cooking videos, but I need to practise making things myself. My cousin has offered to help me on Saturday. We are going to the market to buy fresh ingredients. I am interested in learning simple techniques rather than following difficult recipes immediately. I will remember to prepare everything before turning on the cooker. If the first meal goes well, I hope to cook dinner for my family next weekend.

listening.text: Thanks for considering joining our language exchange. We suggest arriving ten minutes early to meet your partner. Please avoid using your phone during the conversation. Remember to bring a notebook. We look forward to seeing you on Thursday, and we hope to organise another session next month.

questions.why: La sugerencia protege el tiempo de conversación.

units.mission: Explica una decisión y una preferencia usando sus patrones verbales; después pregunta por las de otra persona.

units.title: Comparar opciones
units.goal: Comparar productos, servicios o planes con ventajas, límites y prioridades.

rules.title: Modificar comparativos
rules.text: Usa much, far o a lot para una diferencia grande; a little o slightly para una pequeña. As…as compara igualdad; not as…as expresa inferioridad en una característica.
rules.pattern: much cheaper / slightly larger / as useful as
examples: This option is much cheaper.
The new bag is slightly lighter.
The bus is not as fast as the train.
rules.tip: No combines more con cheaper: no more cheaper.

rules.title: Suficiencia y exceso
rules.text: Too + adjetivo expresa exceso; adjetivo + enough expresa suficiencia. Enough va antes de un nombre. Too expensive no significa simplemente muy caro, sino más de lo aceptable en contexto.
rules.pattern: too heavy / light enough / enough space
examples: The case is too heavy to carry.
This room is large enough for six people.
We do not have enough money.
rules.tip: Very y too no expresan exactamente lo mismo.

rules.title: Justificar una elección
rules.text: Compara según dos o tres criterios relevantes y explica cuál pesa más. Be worth + -ing indica que algo merece el esfuerzo o coste.
examples: The repair is worth considering.
Compared with the train, the bus is cheaper.
Reliability matters more to me than appearance.
rules.tip: Una buena recomendación depende de la necesidad de la persona.

questions.prompt: This bag is ___ lighter than that one.
The bus is not as quick ___ the train.
The box is too heavy ___ alone.

units.story: Mina needed a laptop for writing assignments and attending online classes. One model was much cheaper but had a weak battery. Another was slightly heavier, although it could last all day without charging. Mina rarely worked near a socket, so battery life mattered more to her than weight. A shop assistant suggested an expensive gaming model, but it was too costly and offered features she did not need. Mina chose the middle option after comparing reviews. It was affordable enough and seemed more suitable for her actual routine.

reading.prompt: Which feature mattered most to Mina?
reading.why: A menudo trabaja sin enchufe.

reading.prompt: Why did she reject the gaming model?
reading.answer: It cost too much for features she did not need.
options: It cost too much for features she did not need.
It was cheaper than all the others.
reading.why: La elección se basa en necesidades reales.

dialogue: The middle one is more suitable.
Is it as light as the first one?
No, but the battery lasts much longer.
For my routine, I think it is.
units.writing: Compara dos opciones en 90–120 palabras y recomienda una según una necesidad concreta.
units.model: I would recommend travelling by train for our weekend visit. The bus is slightly cheaper, but the train is much faster and has enough space for our bags. The station is also closer to the museum than the bus stop. For someone with plenty of time, the bus might be a good choice. However, we only have one day, so saving an hour is worth paying a little more. We should book early because the cheapest tickets may sell out before Friday.

listening.text: We have two rooms available. The smaller room costs sixty pounds and faces the main road. The larger room is ten pounds more, but it is much quieter and includes a desk. Both have enough space for two people. Breakfast costs extra in either room.

questions.prompt: How much is the larger room?

questions.answer: It is quieter and has a desk.
options: It is quieter and has a desk.

questions.answer: No, it costs extra in both.
options: No, it costs extra in both.
questions.why: Either room mantiene el coste adicional.

units.mission: Compara dos opciones durante un minuto. Pregunta la prioridad de tu interlocutor antes de recomendar.

units.title: Cantidades y recursos
units.goal: Hablar de cantidades, escasez y distribución con nombres contables e incontables.

rules.title: Contable o incontable
rules.text: Many, a few y fewer acompañan normalmente a nombres contables plurales. Much, a little y less a incontables. Information, advice y equipment suelen ser incontables en inglés.
examples: We need fewer plastic bottles.
There is a little milk left.
She gave me some useful advice.
rules.tip: No añadas -s a advice o information en sus usos habituales.

rules.title: Matices de cantidad
rules.text: A few y a little indican que hay algo disponible. Few y little sin a suelen enfatizar escasez. Plenty of expresa suficiente o abundante; hardly any casi nada.
examples: A few people offered to help.
Few people understood the announcement.
We have plenty of time.
rules.tip: La presencia de a cambia el enfoque positivo o negativo.

rules.title: Distribuir y pedir
rules.text: Each considera elementos individualmente; every presenta el conjunto de forma general. Ambos suelen ir con nombre singular. None significa ninguno o nada según el referente.
examples: Each person can take one notebook.
Every table needs a jug of water.
None of the boxes is empty.
rules.tip: Aprende la cantidad con el nombre al que se refiere.

questions.prompt: We need ___ bottles to reduce waste.
___ people came; the room was almost empty.

units.story: The organisers of a community lunch wanted to avoid wasting food. Instead of preparing the same large portion for everyone, they offered smaller portions and allowed people to ask for more. A few volunteers collected information about dietary needs in advance. Each table had a jug of water, which reduced the number of plastic bottles. There was plenty of rice, but very little salad remained at the end. The team recorded these amounts so that they could plan the next event more accurately. Most guests liked being able to choose how much they ate.

reading.prompt: How did the team reduce waste?
reading.answer: They offered smaller portions with extra available.
options: They offered smaller portions with extra available.
reading.why: La gente podía repetir si lo necesitaba.

reading.prompt: Why did they record the leftovers?
reading.why: Los datos ayudarían a ajustar cantidades.

dialogue: Is there enough food for everyone?
Yes, and there is plenty of rice.
Can each person ask for more?
Of course, if they are still hungry.
units.writing: Escribe un plan de 80–110 palabras para un evento con menos desperdicio. Incluye cinco expresiones de cantidad.
units.model: For our next class lunch, we should ask how many people are coming before buying food. Each person can bring a reusable cup so that we need fewer disposable ones. We should prepare a few different dishes rather than too much of one food. There will be plenty of drinking water, but we only need a little juice. If some food is left, we can offer clean containers for people to take it home. This plan should cost less and help us avoid unnecessary waste.

listening.text: There are a few seats left for the workshop, but hardly any places remain on Saturday. Sunday has more space. Each participant will receive a notebook, so you do not need to bring paper. We have plenty of pens, but please bring your own water bottle.

units.mission: Planifica materiales para un grupo. Aclara qué sobra, qué falta y cómo repartirás los recursos.

units.title: Ideas conectadas
units.goal: Organizar opiniones con razones, ejemplos, contraste y conclusión.

rules.title: Razón y resultado
rules.text: Because introduce una oración; because of un nombre o -ing. So y as a result presentan consecuencias. Usa puntuación para separar las ideas completas con as a result.
examples: We stayed inside because it was raining.
The match stopped because of the rain.
The road was closed, so we took another route.
rules.tip: No escribas because of it was raining.

rules.title: Contraste
rules.text: Although introduce sujeto y verbo. Despite va con nombre o -ing. However conecta ideas completas y necesita puntuación adecuada. No añadas but automáticamente después de although.
examples: Although it was cold, we went out.
Despite the noise, I could concentrate.
It was expensive. However, it lasted for years.
rules.tip: Despite no lleva of en la forma estándar.

rules.title: Párrafos claros
rules.text: Presenta una idea, añade una razón y apóyala con un ejemplo. In addition agrega otro argumento. Una conclusión responde al tema sin introducir una idea totalmente nueva.
examples: In my opinion, libraries are important.
For instance, they offer quiet places to study.
For these reasons, I support the proposal.
rules.tip: Los conectores ayudan, pero no sustituyen una relación lógica real.

questions.prompt: The shop was closed, ___ we went elsewhere.

questions.answer: Although it was late, we called.
options: Although it was late, we called.
Although it was late but we called.
Despite it was late, we called.

units.story: Some residents opposed opening the school library at weekends because they worried about the cost. Others argued that many students had no quiet place to study at home. A volunteer group offered to help with basic tasks, although a trained librarian would still be needed. The school decided to try Saturday opening for one month. Attendance was recorded, and visitors were asked for feedback. As a result, the final decision would be based on actual use rather than guesses. The trial did not settle every question, but it gave both sides useful information.

reading.prompt: What was a concern about weekend opening?
reading.why: Una parte temía gastos adicionales.

reading.prompt: Why organise a trial?
reading.why: La prueba aportaría uso real y opiniones.

dialogue: Yes, because many students need a quiet place.
That is a concern. However, we could try it first.
How would we judge the trial?
We could record attendance and ask for feedback.
units.writing: Escribe una opinión de 100–130 palabras: postura, dos razones, una dificultad y conclusión.
units.model: I think our school should offer a quiet study room after lessons. Some students cannot concentrate at home because of noise or lack of space. In addition, a shared room would make it easier to work on group projects. However, the school would need someone to supervise it. We could begin with two afternoons a week and check how many people use the room. Although this would not solve every problem, it would be a practical first step. For these reasons, I support a short trial before making a permanent decision.

listening.text: Although many people requested a later closing time, the centre will keep its current hours this month because of staff shortages. However, it will open for two extra hours on the first Saturday. Visitors are invited to give feedback after the trial. A final decision will be announced next month.

questions.why: Because of staff shortages da la causa.

questions.answer: Two extra hours on the first Saturday.
options: Two extra hours on the first Saturday.

questions.prompt: When will a final decision be announced?
questions.why: El anuncio será el próximo mes.

units.mission: Defiende una propuesta con dos razones y reconoce una dificultad sin perder tu idea principal.

units.title: Resolver problemas al viajar
units.goal: Pedir información, explicar un contratiempo y negociar una solución.

rules.title: Preguntas indirectas corteses
rules.text: Can you tell me…? y Do you know…? introducen preguntas con orden afirmativo. Para sí/no usa if. Son útiles para pedir ayuda de forma clara y educada.
examples: Can you tell me where the desk is?
Do you know if another train is available?
Could you explain what I should do?
rules.tip: No digas where is the desk dentro de esta pregunta indirecta.

rules.title: Explicar el problema
rules.text: Describe primero la situación, después el efecto y finalmente lo que necesitas. Usa present perfect para un cambio reciente y past simple para detalles terminados.
examples: My flight has been delayed.
I booked this room yesterday.
Could I change my reservation?
rules.tip: Luggage es incontable: some luggage, no luggages.

rules.title: Confirmar soluciones
rules.text: Repite horario, lugar, precio y siguiente paso. So, just to confirm… ayuda a comprobar que ambos entendieron lo mismo.
rules.pattern: Would it be possible…? / just to confirm
examples: Would it be possible to take a later bus?
Is there an extra charge?
So, just to confirm, I should go to platform six.
rules.tip: Una respuesta cortés también debe ser concreta.

questions.prompt: Can you tell me where the station ___?
questions.why: Dentro de la pregunta indirecta se usa orden afirmativo.

questions.prompt: Do you know ___ there is another bus?
Para preguntar por un coste adicional:

units.story: After a late bus caused Eva to miss her train, she went to the information desk. She explained when she had arrived and showed her ticket. The assistant checked the next service and offered two alternatives: a direct train in two hours or an earlier train with a change. Eva was travelling with a large suitcase and preferred the direct route. Before leaving the desk, she confirmed whether her original ticket was still valid and which platform she needed. The journey took longer than planned, but she avoided further confusion by checking the details.

reading.prompt: Why did Eva prefer the later train?
reading.answer: It was direct and easier with her suitcase.
options: It was direct and easier with her suitcase.
It was the only train all week.
reading.why: Quería evitar un cambio con equipaje.

reading.prompt: What did she confirm?
reading.why: Comprobó datos necesarios para continuar.

dialogue: Can you tell me if my ticket is still valid?
Yes, you can use it on the next direct train.
No, there is no extra charge.
Platform six, but check the screen before boarding.
units.writing: Escribe un correo de 80–110 palabras explicando un problema de viaje y pidiendo una solución concreta.
units.model: Dear reservations team, I booked a room for Friday night, but my train has been cancelled and I will arrive on Saturday morning instead. Would it be possible to move my booking to Saturday night? My reservation number is AB123. I would also like to know whether there is an extra charge for changing the date. If the same room is not available, could you suggest a similar option? Please confirm the new arrival time and total price before making the change. Thank you for your help. Kind regards, Alex

listening.text: Passengers for the airport should note that the direct bus is delayed by forty minutes. A train leaves from platform two in fifteen minutes, but you will need to change at Central. Bus tickets are accepted on that train today. Please keep your ticket for the second part of the journey.

questions.prompt: How long is the bus delay?
Can passengers use their bus tickets?
questions.answer: Yes, on the alternative train today.
options: Yes, on the alternative train today.
No, they must buy all new tickets.
questions.why: Se indica la excepción de hoy.

units.mission: Simula una conversación con un servicio de atención: explica el problema, pide dos opciones y confirma la elegida.

units.title: Pedir una solución
units.goal: Presentar una reclamación clara, educada y basada en hechos.

rules.title: Hechos antes que opiniones
rules.text: Explica qué compraste, cuándo y qué falla. Usa pasado para la compra y presente para el problema actual. Evita exagerar o atribuir intenciones que no puedes comprobar.
examples: I bought these headphones last week.
The left speaker does not work.
I have attached a copy of the receipt.
rules.tip: Aporta detalles útiles: modelo, fecha o referencia del pedido.

rules.title: Peticiones corteses
rules.text: I would like + nombre o to + verbo expresa una petición. Could you…? y would it be possible…? permiten solicitar opciones. Preferir una solución no garantiza que esté disponible.
examples: I would like a replacement.
Could you explain the return process?
Would it be possible to collect the item?
rules.tip: No digas I would like that you replace en este patrón.

rules.title: Responder y acordar
rules.text: Reconoce el problema, explica qué puedes hacer y acuerda el siguiente paso. Comprueba plazo y condiciones sin inventar derechos o políticas.
rules.pattern: I am sorry… / We can offer…
examples: I am sorry about the problem.
We can offer a replacement once the item is checked.
Could you confirm the expected delivery date?
rules.tip: Las políticas dependen del comercio y del lugar; pide confirmación.

questions.answer: Would it be possible to replace it?
options: Would it be possible to replace it?

questions.prompt: Para confirmar el siguiente paso pregunta:
questions.answer: When should I expect an update?
options: When should I expect an update?

units.story: Noah ordered a desk lamp for studying. It arrived on time, but the switch did not work properly. He first checked that the cable was connected and followed the instructions. When the problem continued, he contacted customer service with his order number and a description of the fault. The assistant asked for a photograph and offered to arrange a replacement after checking the item. Noah confirmed whether he needed to return the original lamp and kept a copy of the messages. He remained polite while clearly explaining the solution he wanted.

reading.prompt: What did Noah do before contacting support?
reading.answer: He checked the connection and instructions.
options: He checked the connection and instructions.
reading.why: Intentó descartar un problema simple.

reading.prompt: Why did he keep the messages?
reading.answer: To have a record of the agreed steps.
options: To have a record of the agreed steps.
reading.why: Sirven como referencia del acuerdo.

dialogue: My lamp arrived, but the switch is faulty.
Do you have the order number?
Yes, and I can send a photograph.
I would like a working replacement, please.
units.writing: Escribe una reclamación de 90–120 palabras con hechos, comprobaciones realizadas, solución deseada y petición de respuesta.
units.model: Dear customer service team, I received my headphones yesterday, but the microphone does not work. My order number is H204. I have tried them with two devices and checked the settings, but the problem remains. I would like to request a replacement. Could you explain how to return the faulty item and whether I need to include the original packaging? I have attached a copy of the receipt. Please confirm the next step and the expected delivery time for a replacement. Thank you for your assistance. Kind regards, Sam

listening.text: Hello, this is customer support about order K315. We have received your photograph and can arrange a replacement. Please keep the original item until the courier arrives on Thursday. The courier will collect it and bring the new one. If Thursday is inconvenient, reply to our email before Tuesday evening.

questions.prompt: When should the customer request another day?
questions.why: Se indica el límite para cambiar la fecha.

units.mission: Practica los dos papeles: cliente que describe un fallo y agente que propone un siguiente paso.

units.title: Estudio y trabajo
units.goal: Describir capacidades con ejemplos y responder preguntas de una entrevista.

rules.title: Capacidad con evidencia
rules.text: Presenta una habilidad y un ejemplo concreto. Can habla de capacidad actual; managed to describe un logro concreto pasado. Evita listas de cualidades sin mostrar cómo las has usado.
examples: I can organise group tasks.
Last term, I managed to finish a project early.
The experience taught me to ask clear questions.
rules.tip: Un ejemplo pequeño pero real es más útil que una afirmación exagerada.

rules.title: Experiencia y objetivos
rules.text: Present perfect resume experiencia; past simple da detalles. Would like to describe una aspiración de forma cortés. Be responsible for + nombre o -ing especifica funciones.
examples: I have worked with different teams.
I was responsible for checking the list.
I would like to develop my communication skills.
rules.tip: No inventes experiencia para practicar: puedes usar una situación claramente imaginaria.

rules.title: Responder con estructura
rules.text: Ordena una respuesta: situación, tarea, acción y resultado. Después relaciona lo aprendido con el puesto o curso. Para un punto débil, explica también qué haces para mejorarlo.
examples: Our group had a tight deadline.
I divided the work into small tasks.
We finished on time and checked the result together.
rules.tip: No memorices un discurso que no responda a la pregunta real.

questions.prompt: I was responsible for ___ the event.
Last year, I ___ a small team.

questions.why: La evidencia hace la respuesta útil.

questions.answer: What you are doing to improve it.
options: What you are doing to improve it.
A claim that you never make mistakes.

units.story: For her first interview, Hana prepared examples from school projects rather than pretending to have years of work experience. She described organising a charity sale, where she had been responsible for recording payments. When two volunteers were absent, she helped divide the remaining tasks. The interviewer asked what she had found difficult. Hana admitted that she had initially tried to do too much herself. She explained that she was learning to ask for help earlier. Her answers showed both useful experience and a realistic understanding of what she still needed to improve.

reading.prompt: Where did Hana's examples come from?
reading.why: Usó experiencia propia.

reading.prompt: What had she learnt to improve?
reading.why: Reconoció el problema de asumirlo todo.

dialogue: I am organised and can keep accurate records.
I recorded payments at a school event.
What are you working on improving?
I am learning to ask for help before I get overwhelmed.
units.writing: Escribe una presentación para una solicitud de 90–120 palabras. Incluye una habilidad, evidencia, una meta y disponibilidad ficticia o real.
units.model: I would like to apply for the volunteer assistant position at your community centre. I enjoy working with people and have helped organise several school activities. During our last event, I was responsible for checking names and explaining the schedule to visitors. This taught me to stay calm and give clear information. I am also learning to use spreadsheets so that I can manage records more efficiently. I would like to develop these skills while supporting local activities. I am available on Saturday mornings and would welcome the opportunity to discuss the role.

listening.text: Thank you for applying. Your interview will be on Wednesday at eleven. Please bring an example of a project you have worked on; it can be from school or volunteering. You do not need a printed portfolio. We will ask about teamwork and how you deal with unexpected problems.

questions.prompt: What kind of project is acceptable?

questions.why: Do not need elimina la exigencia.

units.mission: Contesta una entrevista breve con ejemplos verificables y una pregunta sobre el puesto o curso.

units.title: Información y tecnología
units.goal: Distinguir hechos, opiniones y afirmaciones pendientes de verificar.

rules.title: Atribuir información
rules.text: According to identifica una fuente; it says that transmite contenido. Distingue lo que observaste de lo que otro afirma. No omitas fechas si cambian el sentido de la información.
examples: According to the notice, the road is closed.
The article says that the event has moved.
I have not checked the original source yet.
rules.tip: Que algo esté publicado no demuestra que sea correcto.

rules.title: Preguntas de comprobación
rules.text: Usa preguntas directas o indirectas para averiguar origen, fecha y evidencia. Before + -ing expresa una acción previa; after + -ing una posterior.
examples: Check the date before sharing the post.
Can you tell me where the image came from?
I want to know whether the claim is accurate.
rules.tip: La pregunta indirecta mantiene orden afirmativo.

rules.title: Resumir con cautela
rules.text: Probably, may y seems expresan grados de certeza. Al resumir, conserva la idea central y omite detalles que no puedes confirmar. Una opinión necesita razones, aunque no sea un hecho comprobable.
examples: This may be an old photograph.
In my opinion, the headline is unclear.
The source does not explain how the figures were collected.
rules.tip: No conviertas may en will al parafrasear: cambia el nivel de certeza.

questions.prompt: ___ the official notice, the event starts at six.
Check the date before ___ the post.
Do you know where the image ___ from?

questions.why: No se debe exagerar la certeza.

questions.prompt: Elige una opinión señalada como tal.
questions.answer: In my opinion, the title is confusing.
