options: In my opinion, the title is confusing.
The notice was published on Monday.

units.story: A photo of a flooded street was shared in a neighbourhood group with a message saying that the town centre was closed. Before changing her route, Elena checked where the image had come from. She found the same photo in an article from three years earlier. The current council notice mentioned repairs on one road, but no flooding. Elena shared the updated notice and explained the date of the old photo without attacking the person who had posted it. Several neighbours thanked her because they had been about to cancel appointments unnecessarily.

reading.prompt: What was misleading about the photo?
reading.answer: It was from an older event.
options: It was from an older event.
reading.why: La fecha cambiaba su interpretación.

reading.prompt: How did Elena correct the information?
reading.answer: She shared a current notice and explained the old date.
options: She shared a current notice and explained the old date.
reading.why: Corrigió con datos y respeto.

dialogue: Not yet. It says the centre is closed.
Do you know when the photo was taken?
I will look for the original source.
What does the current notice say?
Only one road is being repaired.
units.writing: Escribe 90–120 palabras explicando cómo comprobarías una noticia antes de compartirla.
units.model: Before sharing a surprising story, I would check who published it and when it was written. An old report can be misleading if it appears to describe something happening today. I would look for the original source and compare the main claim with other reliable information. If the post included a photograph, I would try to find its earlier use. I would also separate facts from opinions. If I still could not confirm the claim, I would say so clearly instead of presenting it as certain.

listening.text: Please ignore the opening times in yesterday's social media post. They referred to last year's festival. The current programme is available on the organiser's website and was updated this morning. The main exhibition opens at ten, while the evening concert begins at seven. Check the date before sharing a screenshot.

units.mission: Resume una noticia y di qué está confirmado, cuál es la fuente y qué no sabes todavía.

units.title: Colaborar y discrepar
units.goal: Sugerir, discrepar con respeto y llegar a un acuerdo concreto.

rules.title: Sugerencias
rules.text: Suggest + -ing propone una acción. How about + -ing también. Why do not we…? o why don’t we…? usa verbo base. Let us o let’s introduce otra propuesta conjunta.
examples: I suggest meeting earlier.
How about sharing the tasks?
Why do we not ask the group?
rules.tip: Evita suggest to do en este uso.

rules.title: Discrepar con razones
rules.text: I see your point reconoce la idea sin prometer acuerdo. I am not sure that… suaviza una objeción. Explica una razón y ofrece alternativa para avanzar.
examples: I see your point, but time is limited.
I am not sure that this is the fairest option.
Could we try a smaller version first?
rules.tip: Cortesía no significa ocultar lo que necesitas.

rules.title: Cerrar un acuerdo
rules.text: Resume tareas, responsables y plazos. Check back permite verificar si el acuerdo funciona. Aclara palabras ambiguas como soon con una fecha u hora.
examples: I will contact the venue by Friday.
You can check the equipment tomorrow.
Let us review the plan after the first session.
rules.tip: Un acuerdo vago es difícil de cumplir o evaluar.

questions.prompt: Why do we not ___ the group?

questions.answer: I see your point, but I have a concern.
options: I see your point, but I have a concern.

questions.answer: A person, a task and a deadline.
options: A person, a task and a deadline.
questions.why: Permite saber quién hará qué y cuándo.

units.story: The school magazine team disagreed about its next issue. One group wanted more sports stories, while another preferred art and music. The editor asked everyone to explain what readers might gain from each topic. Instead of choosing one group as the winner, the team agreed to include a shorter section for each interest and ask readers for feedback. They divided the writing tasks and set a date for first drafts. The discussion took longer than expected, but the final plan was clearer because each person knew what they were responsible for.

reading.prompt: How did the team resolve the disagreement?
reading.answer: They included different interests and planned feedback.
options: They included different interests and planned feedback.
reading.why: Buscaron un acuerdo intermedio.

reading.prompt: What made the plan clear?
reading.answer: Tasks and draft dates were assigned.
options: Tasks and draft dates were assigned.
Only one person knew the plan.
reading.why: Se concretaron responsabilidades.

dialogue: I think we should focus on sport.
I see your point, but some readers prefer music.
How about including a short section for each?
Who will prepare the first drafts?
I will write about music by Friday.
units.writing: Escribe un mensaje de 90–120 palabras resolviendo un desacuerdo de grupo, con propuesta y tareas concretas.
units.model: Hi team, I understand that some of you want to film outdoors, while others are worried about the weather. I suggest filming the opening scene in the park and the longer conversations inside. This would give us interesting images without depending on good weather all day. Could we try this plan on Saturday? I will check the indoor room by Thursday, and Sara can confirm who is available. Please send any concerns before Friday evening. After the first session, we can review what worked and change the remaining plan if necessary.

listening.text: Following our discussion, we have agreed to hold two shorter meetings instead of one long session. The first will be online on Monday, and the second will be in person on Thursday. Please send your ideas before Sunday evening. Jo will prepare a short summary so that we can use meeting time for decisions.

questions.prompt: Why will Jo prepare a summary?
questions.answer: To leave meeting time for decisions.
options: To leave meeting time for decisions.

units.mission: Negocia una decisión con otra persona: escucha, discrepa si hace falta y termina con un acuerdo verificable.

units.title: Recomendar una experiencia
units.goal: Describir una experiencia cultural y recomendarla a un público concreto.

rules.title: Describir y reaccionar
rules.text: Los adjetivos en -ing suelen describir lo que provoca una emoción; los de -ed cómo se siente alguien. No es una regla sobre personas frente a cosas: una persona también puede ser interesting.
examples: The story was moving.
I felt moved by the ending.
The performance was disappointing.
rules.tip: I am bored significa estoy aburrido; I am boring significa que resulto aburrido.

rules.title: Reseñar con límites
rules.text: Identifica obra o experiencia, describe sin contar todos los detalles y explica ventajas o límites. Recommend + nombre o -ing es un patrón útil.
examples: I recommend visiting the exhibition.
The story takes place in a small village.
It would appeal to people who enjoy mysteries.
rules.tip: No reveles el final si la persona quiere descubrirlo por sí misma.

rules.title: Adecuar al público
rules.text: Una recomendación útil indica a quién le conviene y por qué. Usa although para un límite y especially para destacar una parte. Diferencia tu gusto de un hecho universal.
examples: I especially enjoyed the live music.
Although it was long, I stayed interested.
I would recommend it to families with older children.
rules.tip: Incluye razones concretas, no solo good o bad.

questions.why: La persona expresa cómo se sintió.
Describe el efecto de la charla.

questions.prompt: The story takes ___ in a village.

questions.answer: Although it was long, I enjoyed it.
options: Although it was long, I enjoyed it.
Despite it was long, I enjoyed it.
A promise everyone will love it.

units.story: Kai visited a small exhibition about life near the coast. He expected only photographs, but the exhibition also included recorded interviews and objects donated by local families. The stories about fishing and storms were moving, although some recordings were difficult to hear when the room became busy. Kai especially enjoyed a map showing how the town had changed. He would recommend the exhibition to people interested in local history, but he suggested visiting early in the day. His review explained both what he liked and one practical limitation.

reading.prompt: What surprised Kai?
reading.answer: There were interviews and objects as well as photos.
options: There were interviews and objects as well as photos.
The exhibition was a sports match.
reading.why: El formato era más amplio de lo esperado.

reading.prompt: Why did he suggest an early visit?
reading.answer: Recordings were harder to hear in a busy room.
options: Recordings were harder to hear in a busy room.
reading.why: Relaciona la recomendación con el ruido.

dialogue: Yes, especially if you enjoy local history.
The room became noisy, so I would go early.
units.writing: Escribe una reseña de 90–120 palabras con descripción, dos valoraciones, una limitación y público recomendado.
units.model: I recently visited a small science exhibition with a friend. It included practical experiments as well as short videos explaining everyday technology. I especially enjoyed the section about sound because visitors could compare different vibrations. The explanations were clear, although some activities had long queues. I would recommend visiting early and allowing at least two hours. The exhibition would suit families and anyone who enjoys learning by trying things. It was not a quiet experience, but I left feeling interested and ready to read more about the topics we had explored.

listening.text: I enjoyed the new play at the community theatre. The actors were convincing, and the live music created a warm atmosphere. However, the first half was quite slow. I would recommend it to people who enjoy family stories rather than fast action. If you go, choose a seat near the centre to hear the quieter dialogue.

questions.why: La recomendación se basa en escuchar mejor.

units.mission: Recomienda una película, libro o lugar. Explica a quién podría gustarle y una limitación sin revelar todo.

units.title: Tu proyecto final B1
units.goal: Combinar narración, opinión, planificación y resolución de problemas con autonomía.

rules.title: Elegir tiempos por significado
rules.text: Usa pasado para una experiencia terminada, perfect para lo aprendido hasta ahora y formas futuras para próximos pasos. Revisa cada cambio de tiempo según lo que quieres comunicar.
examples: Last month, I organised a small event.
I have learnt to explain my ideas more clearly.
Next time, I am going to prepare an alternative.
rules.tip: No cambies de tiempo al azar dentro de la misma secuencia.

rules.title: Dar razones y responder
rules.text: Presenta una opinión, da evidencia y reconoce un límite. Al escuchar una pregunta, comprueba qué se pide. Puedes reformular o pedir aclaración sin perder el turno.
examples: I think the plan worked because more people joined.
However, we did not have enough time.
Could you clarify what you mean by successful?
rules.tip: No necesitas entender cada palabra para pedir una aclaración útil.

rules.title: Revisar con criterio

units.story: At the end of her English course, Mari prepared a presentation about a neighbourhood book exchange. She explained why she had joined, what the group had achieved and which problems remained. During practice, she noticed that her slides contained too much text, so she replaced some paragraphs with key words. A classmate asked how the project could continue without regular donations. Mari did not have a complete answer, but she described two possibilities and admitted what still needed checking. Her teacher praised the clear organisation and suggested practising shorter pauses between ideas.

units.writing: Proyecto: escribe 120–160 palabras sobre una experiencia, lo aprendido, una opinión razonada y un plan futuro. Revisa organización y tiempos.
units.model: Last month, I helped organise a book exchange at our community centre. At first, we expected only a few visitors, but more than thirty people came. I was responsible for explaining how the exchange worked and helping children choose books. Since then, I have become more confident about speaking to unfamiliar people. In my opinion, small community events are valuable because they connect neighbours who might not otherwise meet. However, we needed clearer signs, and some visitors were confused about where to leave their books. If we repeat the event, I will prepare a simple map and ask another volunteer to welcome people at the door. I am also going to collect feedback after the next exchange so that our decisions are based on what visitors actually need.

listening.text: For your final presentation, choose a familiar experience or project. Speak for two minutes, explaining what happened, what you learnt and what you would change. You may use a card with key words, but please do not read a full script. Afterwards, a partner will ask two questions. Give reasons and examples in your answers.

pronunciation: Después de sonidos sordos distintos de /t/, -ed suele sonar /t/. No añadas una sílaba extra: watched tiene una sílaba.
Después de sonidos sonoros distintos de /d/, -ed suele sonar /d/, sin sílaba extra.
Tras /t/ o /d/, -ed añade una sílaba: wanted y needed tienen dos.
La -s puede sonar /s/ o /z/. En watches y changes aparece una sílaba adicional /ɪz/. Escucha y conserva la terminación.
/ɪ/ y /iː/ no se distinguen solo por duración: cambia también la posición de la lengua. Escucha palabras completas.
Las terminaciones -teen y -ty pueden confundirse. Escucha también la consonante final y confirma los números importantes.
I can come. · I cannot come.
Can suele reducirse cuando no lleva énfasis. No dependas solo de oír una /t/ final para identificar can’t: usa contexto y pide confirmación.
Could you repeat that? · Where do you live?
Escucha la frase por grupos y repite conservando el significado. La entonación varía con intención y acento; no hay una única melodía correcta.
Estos pares difieren por vocal y según el acento también por la /r/. Compara la voz británica y estadounidense disponible.
El acento principal cae al principio en estas palabras. Algunas sílabas débiles se reducen en el habla; busca claridad sin pronunciar todo con igual fuerza.
checklist: Explicar hábitos, cambios y estrategias de aprendizaje con razones.
Narrar una experiencia distinguiendo la acción principal, el contexto y un hecho anterior.
Relacionar experiencias con el presente y pedir detalles sobre momentos terminados.
Expresar duración, actividad reciente y resultados cuantificables.
Comparar hábitos anteriores con nuevas situaciones y procesos de adaptación.
Distinguir intenciones, acuerdos, decisiones y condiciones temporales futuras.
Explicar resultados habituales y posibilidades futuras con condiciones.
Explorar situaciones hipotéticas y dar consejos razonados.
Distinguir obligaciones, prohibiciones, opciones y recomendaciones.
Expresar certeza y posibilidad a partir de indicios sin confundirlas con hechos.
Describir procesos y hechos poniendo el foco en la acción o el resultado.
Resumir lo que otra persona dijo, pidió o preguntó.
Identificar personas, objetos y lugares usando oraciones de relativo.
Usar verbos con infinitivo o -ing en planes, preferencias y propósitos.
Comparar productos, servicios o planes con ventajas, límites y prioridades.
Hablar de cantidades, escasez y distribución con nombres contables e incontables.
Organizar opiniones con razones, ejemplos, contraste y conclusión.
Pedir información, explicar un contratiempo y negociar una solución.
Presentar una reclamación clara, educada y basada en hechos.
Describir capacidades con ejemplos y responder preguntas de una entrevista.
Distinguir hechos, opiniones y afirmaciones pendientes de verificar.
Sugerir, discrepar con respeto y llegar a un acuerdo concreto.
Describir una experiencia cultural y recomendarla a un público concreto.
Combinar narración, opinión, planificación y resolución de problemas con autonomía.
